points.description: States that introducing non-linearity into the features (nonlinear transformation of feature vectors) lets models learn/capture much more complex data patterns (complex, non-linearly separable structure).
points.partial_credit: Half only if it says non-linear transformation helps with complex data but does not clearly state that models can learn complex patterns.

points.description: States that nonlinear features can be used with very basic (simple/linear) classifiers, such as an SVM, to classify very complex data sets efficiently and effectively.
points.partial_credit: Half if it says simple classifiers can classify complex data but names no basic classifier such as SVM or omits efficiency/effectiveness.

rubric.notes: Full marks need both ideas stated precisely: nonlinearity lets models learn complex patterns, and simple classifiers like SVM then work effectively on complex data. Vague statements such as "improves accuracy" or "makes data better" earn nothing. A wrong claim on a point (for example, that nonlinear transformation simplifies or reduces the data) means that point earns nothing.
